## Linear Programming Model


$$
\begin{array}{lrll}
    \max & \sum\limits_{j=1}^nc_jx_j\\
    &\sum\limits_{j=1}^n a_{ij}x_j&\leq b_i,& i=1,\ldots,m\\
    &x_j&\geq 0,& j=1,\ldots,n
\end{array}
$$ {#eq-ob}

@eq-ob is a linear programming model with $n$ decision variables $x_j$ and $m$
constraints. The coefficients $c_j$ represent the contribution of each variable
to the objective, while $a_{ij}$ and $b_i$ define the constraints.


We simulate data.

```{python}
#| label: fig-mat
#| fig-cap: "Simulated data for the constraint matrix."

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
n = 20
m = 10

A = rng.uniform(0, 10, (m, n))

print(A)

plt.figure(figsize=(5, 6))
plt.imshow(A, aspect="auto", interpolation="nearest", cmap="viridis")
plt.colorbar(label="Value")
plt.xlabel("Column")
plt.ylabel("Constraint Index")
#plt.xticks([0, 1], ["Intercept", "x"])
plt.title("Constraint matrix A")
plt.show()
```

## Results

As shown in @fig-mat, the estimates are
$n =$ `{python} f"{A.shape[1]:.2f}"` and
$m =$ `{python} f"{A.shape[0]:.2f}"`.
